deities: Lord Krishna as Mathuradheesh (Lord of Mathura); an idol of Radha stands beside Krishna per some sources

history.dynasty: Hada Rajputs; the Kota rulers - notably Maharao Bhim Singh I (r. 1707-1720) - patronized and promoted Vaishnavism
history.summary: A major Krishna temple in old Kota (Patanpole area), belonging to the Pushtimarg (Vallabha) Sampradaya - regarded as the Pratham Peeth (first seat) of the Vallabh Kul in Kota. The deity's idol was brought to Kota from the Mathura region - visitor accounts differ on the exact origin: Jatipura near Govardhan (Mathura) versus Karnaval village near Mathura - flag this conflict as unverified; one review says it was placed in the haveli of Dewan Dwarka Das (verify). The presiding murti of Mathuradheeshji (Krishna, the Lord of Mathura) is described as a neelam (blue sapphire/gem) stone idol (visitor report - verify). Built in traditional North Indian Nagara style with intricately carved shikharas, pillars, mandapas and Bhagavata Purana/Krishna-leela carvings; a ghat near the Chambal River adds to the complex (placeapp - verify). Coordinates are from map geocode of 'Shuddhadvait Pratham Peeth, Patan Road, Bhatt Ji Ghat, Kaithunipole, Kota'.

name: Mathuradheesh Temple
town_description: Kota is a major city on the Chambal River in southeastern Rajasthan, best known nationally as India's coaching-education hub. On the Chambal's banks it also holds a string of old temples - Khade Ganesh Ji, the Mathuradheesh Temple of the old city, and the ancient Kansua Shiv Mandir - set around riverside gardens, the Chambal Garden and the old Patanpole quarter.

travel.railway: Kota Junction - major Delhi-Mumbai line station (verify distance to temple).
travel.road: In the old city near Patanpole/Kaithunipole; easily reached by city taxi or auto (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Janmashtami is the busiest and most vibrant time.
